title: Wertheim National Wildlife Refuge
summary: Wertheim National Wildlife Refuge protects habitat along the Carmans River in Shirley and houses the Long Island National Wildlife Refuge Complex visitor center. Inside, an interpretive section shares Unkechaug Nation history and displays objects connected with that history. At the center's November 2011 dedication, representatives of the Unkechaug and Shinnecock Nations offered a traditional blessing, recognizing enduring Native relationships with the river, wetlands, and wildlife.

why_this_matters: Wertheim is not only a protected river and wetland landscape. Its visitor center makes Unkechaug Nation history visible to the public, while the 2011 blessing by Unkechaug and Shinnecock representatives recognized continuing Native relationships with the Carmans River, wetlands, and wildlife.
preservation_content: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service manages Wertheim as part of the Long Island National Wildlife Refuge Complex. The visitor center includes an interpretive section sharing Unkechaug Nation history and displaying objects connected with that history. At the November 2011 dedication, Unkechaug and Shinnecock representatives offered a traditional blessing.
artifacts_title: Unkechaug Nation history inside the visitor center
artifacts_content: Inside the public visitor center, an interpretive section presents Unkechaug Nation history and displays objects connected with that history. The exhibit gives visitors a present-day place to encounter this history while visiting the refuge and Carmans River landscape.
